text:
marta: quick flag — dashboard p99 for POST /v1/generate?stream=true spikes while p50/p95 stay flat. looks like the panel mixes streaming vs non-streaming latencies. snapshot: global p50=140ms p95=310ms p99=720ms; stream=true p50=142ms p95=315ms p99=2.4s :thinking:

oren: are we measuring TTFB or total time for stream endpoints in our rollups?

marta: not sure, digging. no infra changes in that window.

ty: we historically added ttfb_ms for streaming (first-chunk) and total_ms for full responses. ingestion normalizes into a single latency_ms field but with a precedence rule.
ingest-bot: ingestion note: latency_ms = first_non_null(total_ms, request_duration_ms, ttfb_ms). (see docs/telemetry/latency_normalization.md)

marta: that precedence means some stream requests contribute ttfb while others contribute total — mixing two different distributions. small fraction of full responses (long tail) can blow up p99 when slice reduces sample size.

oren: interesting. we should verify by grouping on which raw field was used. run something like:

```
SELECT minute, count(*) n, pctl(0.99, latency_ms) p99, coalesce(raw_total_ms IS NOT NULL, raw_ttfb_ms IS NOT NULL) AS latency_type
FROM requests
WHERE endpoint='/v1/generate' AND stream=true
GROUP BY minute, latency_type
ORDER BY minute DESC
LIMIT 30;
```

ty: better: derive a string flag 'latency_type' = CASE WHEN raw_total_ms IS NOT NULL THEN 'total' WHEN raw_ttfb_ms IS NOT NULL THEN 'ttfb' ELSE 'unknown' END and group by that.

marta: ran grouped query — p99 spikes align with minutes where ~1% of samples reported "total" (full responses) with latencies 1.1s-3.6s; majority are ttfb ~150-350ms. histogram fallback + mixed types explains UI p99 blowup.

ty: two quick UX fixes: 1) show "latency_provenance" badge near p99 (total/ttfb/normalized) + sample_count; 2) auto-suggest "split by latency_type" when mixed provenance detected. low effort.

oren: medium-term: change ingestion so latency_ms consistently uses total_ms for SLO-facing panels and expose ttfb as a separate metric for streaming UX. SLOs usually care about total time to close.

marta: agree. additionally, add a confidence indicator when p99 is computed over mixed latency types or on histogram-derived rollups with small sample_count. e.g., confidence=low if mixed_types OR sample_count<2500 and provenance=histogram.

console: created CONSOLE-6005: "Expose latency_type provenance for streaming endpoints + split-by action + SLO default to total_ms". Attached queries and screenshots.

ty: implementation notes: API could accept param `latency_mode=total|ttfb|normalized` so console can explicitly request which latency to show. Also add quick action to fetch per-latency-type percentiles via `/api/metrics/percentiles?by=latency_type`.

marta: that'll help on-call triage a lot. tagging @ty @oren. I'll attach the raw rows from the spike minutes to CONSOLE-6005 and mark for priority since it's causing false alarms.

oren: one more: for streaming panels default UX show both metrics side-by-side: p50/p95 on ttfb, p99 on total with provenance badge. reduces confusion.

marta: good idea. I'll include mock in the ticket. closing thread for now — thanks all :raised_hands:
